subject: US-West maintenance: staggered driver hotfix & service handovers (planning + customer ops)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Turner <leah.turner@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, CloudHub Partner Ops <partner-ops@cloudhub.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:00:00 +0000
Subject: US-West maintenance: staggered driver hotfix & service handovers (planning + customer ops)

Leah / Acme team —

Quick heads-up: we’re scheduling a staggered maintenance window in us-west next week to deploy a driver hotfix that addresses a rare GPU memory regression we observed in heavy batch tails. We designed the rollout as a sequence of short rolling restarts with customer-facing handovers so that customer workloads see minimal disruption.

High-level plan (short):
- Window: Tue 18 Aug, 02:00–06:00 PDT (09:00–13:00 UTC) — staggered across AZs, each AZ ~15–25 minute drain+restart.
- Canary: start with 3% of traffic on a dedicated canary pool for first 45 minutes, then expand.
- Impact: expected transient token-generation latency spikes (seconds) during per-AZ handover; no sustained errors expected.
- Fallback: automatic routing to warm standby pool in another AZ if any node fails health checks.
- Post-op: we’ll publish a short postmortem and the canary telemetry dashboard.

Attachments: maintenance notice PDF and the canary runbook (internal). Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2026-08-uswest-hotfix

Action items for you: if you have any scheduled large inference jobs spanning that window, please let us know by EOD Mon 17 Aug so we can schedule them away from the canary bursts. If you’d like us to opt your account into a quieter canary (zero active canary until expansion), tell us and we’ll do that.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Regional Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: uswest-driver-hotfix-notice-20260812.pdf (PDF, 1 page); canary-runbook-uswest.xlsx (XLSX, internal runbook)

Will the canary or any AZ handover risk causing dropped requests or queue timeouts for that window? We can shift it but want to understand the expected behavior if we leave it.

Leah
Leah Turner

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 18:12, Leah Turner <leah.turner@acmeai.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads-up, Jonas. Quick question — our nightly batch inference job runs 03:30–04:30 PDT and ingests ~120k requests. Will the canary or any AZ handover risk causing dropped requests or queue timeouts for that window?

Good question — short answer: no expected dropped requests. More detail:
- During a per-AZ drain we gracefully stop accepting new work on affected workers and route new requests to healthy nodes; in-flight requests on preempted workers are allowed to finish where possible.
- We have a small window where queued requests may see increased latency; that can push into your request timeout if you’ve set a very tight client-side deadline. We’ll set client-side guidance to 45s for the affected window.
- For large batch runs we can proactively route your traffic to the warm standby pool for the 03:00–05:00 PDT period; this will keep latency stable but may slightly increase overall cost for that night.

If you want us to route Acme AI to standby for that period I can arrange it — please confirm by EOD Mon 17 Aug.

-Jonas
